subtype: Signs a friend or family may notice [Observer]
passage:
Dhruv: hey didi, Maa's birthday lunch sunday? 1 pm at home
Nikita: will ask Varun and tell u
Dhruv: ok. u used to just say yes
Nikita: things are different now
Nikita: can u send me 200 for the auto? will return
Dhruv: sent. didn't u get salary last week?
Nikita: Varun handles the account now. it's easier
Dhruv: ok. how are u really?
Nikita: fine. have to go, he wants my location when i leave office
Dhruv: no lecture, promise. just know i'm here. any time, any hour
Dhruv: and if u ever want, i can come get u. no questions
Nikita: thanks bhai
Nikita: don't tell Maa about the 200
Dhruv: i won't. see u sunday i hope

qa.q: How much did Nikita ask Dhruv to send for the auto?
qa.a: Nikita asked Dhruv to send 200 for the auto.

qa.q: What might Dhruv be worried about when he asks "how are u really?"
qa.a: He is worried that Nikita has lost control of her own money and plans, since she now needs Varun's say and must share her location.

qa.q: Which of Dhruv's messages was wise, and why?
qa.a: Promising no lecture and offering to come any time, no questions, keeps Nikita connected without blame, so she has a safe person if she needs help.

qa.q: What might it be like for Nikita to read "i can come get u. no questions"?
qa.a: It may bring quiet relief, a sign that someone will help without judging her or pushing her to leave before she is ready.

grounding: A younger brother notices his sister now asks permission, has lost access to her salary and reports her location, and stays in touch without blame.

subtype: Signs a friend or family may notice [Observer]
passage:
Chinmay hadn't seen his sister Jasleen in six months, though her in-laws' house was only two bus stops past the mandi.
She opened the door smiling too brightly. Her husband, Gurmeet, sat on the charpai with her phone in his hand.
Over tea, Chinmay noticed things. Jasleen glanced at Gurmeet before answering even simple questions. She said she had given up her tailoring work for the house. When Chinmay mentioned Bebe's birthday next week, Gurmeet said, "We'll see," and Jasleen said nothing.
At the gate, alone for a minute, Chinmay didn't say leave him, or why do you put up with this. He knew pushing could drive her further in.
He said, "I'll call every Sunday at eleven. If you don't pick up, I'll just call again. Bebe and I are always there. Any time."
Jasleen squeezed his hand hard, once, and went inside.

qa.q: How far was Jasleen's in-laws' house?
qa.a: It was only two bus stops past the mandi.

qa.q: What does Jasleen's glance at Gurmeet before answering suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she feels watched and anxious, checking whether each answer is allowed.

qa.q: Why was Chinmay's promise at the gate a wise choice?
qa.a: Instead of blaming or pushing her to leave, he set a steady Sunday call and said he and Bebe are always there, keeping a safe line open.

qa.q: What might Jasleen's hard squeeze of his hand mean?
qa.a: It may mean gratitude and a silent sign that something is wrong, even though she cannot say it out loud there.

grounding: A brother visiting his sister notices her anxious glances, lost work and a husband holding her phone, and keeps in touch without blame rather than pushing her to leave.
